Hey everyone!  I'm Ayesha from Pakistan and I'm tackling the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge. I’m building an interactive map UI to help astronauts navigate Mars, track routes and check environmental data. I have the visuals covered but I need a partner for the backend.
Looking for: A Backend Developer who can work with APIs, databases, or process NASA’s spatial datasets. If you want to build an awesome prototype this weekend, request to join AbandonedBuilder!
summary:
AresPath: An Interactive Martian Surface Mapping and Exploration Platform

AresPath is a web-based Martian mapping platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026's “Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map” challenge. It brings Mars surface data into an interactive interface to help users explore regions of interest and understand the terrain that future astronauts may encounter during surface exploration.

The platform focuses on the Jezero Crater region and integrates available NASA-derived terrain datasets, including a 20-meter Digital Elevation Model (DEM). Through its interactive map interface and layer-based visualization, users can examine Martian surface information and explore the potential for safer, more informed route planning.

AresPath addresses the challenge by making scientific terrain data more accessible and presenting it in a practical exploration-focused environment. This is important because future human missions to Mars will require reliable knowledge of surface conditions to support navigation, destination selection, and mission planning. AresPath provides a foundation for integrating additional datasets and advanced astronaut route-planning capabilities as they become available.
details: AresPath is an interactive web-based Martian surface exploration platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It focuses on the Jezero Crater region and helps users explore Martian terrain through an interactive map and available data layers. The platform integrates a 20-meter Digital Elevation Model (DEM), allowing users to examine elevation variations and better understand the Martian landscape. AresPath uses a frontend-backend architecture. The frontend is built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and MapLibre, while the backend uses Python and FastAPI to provide regional information, layer metadata, and terrain-related API responses. The application is deployed using Vercel and Render, with Git and GitHub used for version control. Understanding Martian terrain is important for future human missions because elevation and surface conditions can affect astronaut mobility, destination selection, and mission safety. AresPath aims to make planetary terrain information more accessible and provide a foundation for data-informed exploration planning. Our creative approach is to transform scientific Mars datasets into an accessible interactive exploration experience. The platform is designed to be modular and expandable, with future potential for additional imagery, slope analysis, hazard identification, and terrain-aware route planning. These capabilities could help mission planners evaluate exploration areas and make safer decisions for future astronaut missions.
